definition: The authors used the tool for their own analysis: fitting, estimation, simulation with their model, or the tool is the platform their new method runs in, or their software is built around the tool.

The tool is a benchmark or reference that the authors' own method or tool is compared with (for example "compared with SCM in Monolix", "results agreed with NONMEM"), including a tool the authors run only to produce the reference results their method is compared with.
The tool is named only in passing: background, a list of software, an example of what others use, future work.
